name: Kozhundeeswarar Temple, Tirukkottur
deity: Shiva as Kozhundeeswarar, with the goddess Madhuravasanaambikai
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Kottur, near Mannargudi in the Tiruvarur delta, honours Shiva as Kozhundeeswarar with the goddess Madhuravasanaambikai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar — the 111th shrine of the Kaveri's southern bank — it is revered as a guru-sthalam, where the lord and the goddess face one another.

sections.history: Kottur, with the historical name Indirapuram, lies about 15 km from Mannargudi and 27 km from Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, and counted the 111th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. Its inscriptions name Raja Raja Chola I, Rajadhiraja I and Kulothunga Chola III, and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Kozhundeeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Madhuravasanaambikai — also Thenmozhippaavai — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sanctums of Shiva and the goddess are set facing one another, an arrangement for which the temple is revered as a guru-sthalam. The walled courtyard keeps the form of the Shiva temples of the Tiruvarur delta.
sections.legends: The sthala legend recalls the demon Vritrasura and the vajra, the thunderbolt weapon made from the spine of the sage Dadichi, by which he was overcome. Shiva is worshipped here as Kozhundeeswarar, with the goddess Madhuravasanaambikai beside him; because the lord and the goddess face each other, the shrine is held a guru-sthalam. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Mannargudi tract include Kottur among their stops, for the guru-sthalam's sake.
sections.experience: At Kottur the pilgrim comes to the guru-sthalam of the delta. Before Kozhundeeswarar and Madhuravasanaambikai — who face one another across the shrine — in the country near Mannargudi, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple and the memory of Dadichi's gift that overcame Vritrasura.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Kottur lies about 15 km from Mannargudi and 27 km from Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district. Mannargudi and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
